title: 2010 AMC 12B 16
statement: Positive integers \(a,\) \(b,\) and \(c\) are randomly and independently selected with replacement from the set \(\{1, 2, 3, \ldots, 2010\}.\) What is the probability that \(abc+ab+a\) is divisible by \(3?\)

solutions.text:
Factor \(abc+ab+a=a(bc+b+1).\) Since \(2010\) is a multiple of \(3,\) each of \(a, b, c\) is uniform modulo \(3.\)

If \(a\) is divisible by \(3\) (probability \(\tfrac13\)), the product is divisible by \(3.\)

If \(a\) is not divisible by \(3\) (probability \(\tfrac23\)), we need \(bc+b+1\) to be divisible by \(3.\) Checking residues, this holds exactly when \((b,c)\equiv(1,1)\) or \((2,0)\pmod3,\) a probability of \(\tfrac13\cdot\tfrac13+\tfrac13\cdot\tfrac13=\tfrac29.\)

The total probability is \[ \frac13+\frac23\cdot\frac29=\frac13+\frac{4}{27}=\frac{13}{27}. \]

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Factor \(abc+ab+a=a(bc+b+1);\) each residue mod \(3\) is equally likely
If \(a\) is divisible by \(3\) it works; otherwise require \(bc+b+1\) to be divisible by \(3\)
